text:
A: Hello, er, can you see me alright?
B: Yeah. Yeah, I can.
A: Good stuff. I'm Callum. I'm in Taunton, down in Somerset.
B: Joanne. St Helens.
A: St Helens, right. Rugby league, isn't it?
B: Yeah. My husband's Saints mad. I'm not bothered, I just know the score.
A: Ha, fair. I'm a bit like that with the cricket. I go to the County Ground but I'm mostly there for the cider, you know.
B: Yeah.
A: So, er, what do you do, Joanne?
B: I'm not working at the minute. I look after me mum. She's got dementia, early stages, so it's sort of a full-time thing now.
A: Oh, sorry. That must be hard work.
B: It is, yeah. I was in a warehouse eleven years, food packing in Haydock. I gave it up three years ago. She lives four streets away, so I'm back and forth all day. Tablets, appointments, ringing the surgery at eight o'clock to get through. You spend half your life on hold.
A: Is it like, they don't call you back sort of thing?
B: They don't. Or they ring when I'm at hers and I can't answer. I'm blunt with them now. I weren't before, but you have to be.
A: Yeah, I bet. My mum'd be the same. Sorry, I'm not comparing, I just mean she'd be like a dog with a bone.
B: No, it's alright. What do you do?
A: I'm a joiner. Windows, doors, repairs on old houses mostly. We're doing this big Victorian one at the minute, and when we took the panelling off, the original shutters were still in there, folded back into the walls. Nobody'd known for, like, a hundred years. Proper lovely they are, still work and everything. I was dead chuffed. Sorry, I'm going on.
B: No, that's interesting. Me dad was at the glassworks. He liked old things like that.
A: Pilkington's?
B: Yeah.
A: Oh nice. Old glass is lovely, the wavy stuff in sashes. We try and save it when we can. Is your dad still about?
B: No, he died when I was thirty.
A: Ah. Sorry.
B: It's alright. Long time ago now.
A: Yeah.
B: Do you live on your own, then?
A: Er, no. Back at my mum and stepdad's, to be honest. Split up with my girlfriend a couple of years back, gave up the flat. Thirty and in my old bedroom. Not where I thought I'd be, but they're good about it. My stepdad's the one got me into wood, so I've taken half his garage over.
B: Nowt wrong with that. Better than paying some landlord.
A: That's what my mum says. Meant to be saving. Going alright, sort of.
B: I've never lived more than three mile from where I grew up, so I can't talk.
A: Do you get away at all?
B: Not since me mum's diagnosis. We used to go to a caravan in Prestatyn. I worry something'll happen if I'm not there.
A: Yeah, that makes sense. Wales is nice though, I camp in Wales a fair bit. You'll get back there.
B: Maybe. That puzzle at the start, did you finish it?
A: Not really, no. The shapes ones did my head in.
B: Me too. I like a word search, me. That was something else.
A: Ha, yeah. Give me a set of drawings and I'm fine, but those little...
